question:
(a) Explain how nuclear force is responsible for binding nucleons inside a nucleus.
(b) Why is energy required to separate a nucleus into individual nucleons? Relate your answer to binding energy.

options.A:
(a) Strong short-range attractive nuclear force binds protons and neutrons and overcomes proton-proton repulsion at nuclear distances.
(b) Separating nucleons requires work against this attraction. This energy is the binding energy, $E_b=\Delta mc^2$.
options.B:
(a) Nuclear force is repulsive and separates nucleons.
(b) No energy is required to separate a nucleus because its mass is greater than the sum of nucleon masses.
options.C:
(a) Only electrons bind nucleons inside the nucleus.
(b) Binding energy is the energy released when the nucleus is separated.
options.D:
(a) Gravitation is responsible for nuclear binding.
(b) Binding energy is $E_b=mc$, where $m$ is electron mass.
